A teratogenic effect refers to the adverse effects on the development of the embryo or fetus when a pregnant woman is exposed to certain substances, chemicals, or other agents. The term "teratogen" comes from the Greek words "teratos" (monster) and "gen" (producing), essentially meaning "monster-producing."

Teratogens can cause birth defects and developmental abnormalities in the unborn child. Examples of known teratogenic substances include certain medications (like thalidomide), alcohol, some infections, and various chemicals.

Looking at the options:
A. Effect of development of the children - This refers to effects on children after birth
B. Effect on Genes - This would be more accurately described as mutagenic effects
C. Effect on individual organ in the body - This is too narrow; teratogens affect fetal development broadly
D. Effect on rate of cell mutation in the body - This describes mutagenic effects
E. Effect on the unborn child - This correctly describes teratogenic effects

The correct answer is E.
